pages.title: Surgical Gloving
pages.scope: Complete original and rewritten MDX read, including every table, practical summary, cross-link and reference. Consequential recommendations checked against original trial/consensus text, official guidance and available primary abstracts. No product-specific glove validation or clinician sign-off.
changes: Replaced examination-glove material rankings and generic nitrile default with sterile surgical product selection, fit and specific allergy formulation.
Replaced a 2009 review supporting a 2017 regulatory event with the FDA page and actual final rule.
Corrected sterile assistant versus circulator roles; qualified small donning simulations as contamination-surrogate evidence.

Removed universal any-incision standard-of-care attribution and no-dexterity-penalty guarantee. Preserved Cochrane occupational barrier benefit, person-operation denominator and imprecise needlestick evidence.
Aligned Enz 2026 with its conditional double-gloving and 60–120-minute single/outer-glove statements, unresolved inner-glove timing and manufacturer-funded consensus design.
Removed falsely mandated WSES 90-minute timing and universal 240-minute inner-glove reassurance.
Removed denominator-mismatched specialty perforation comparisons, broad 10–63%/78–100% rates and unjustified strongest-predictor ranking.

Expanded high-yield ChEETAh evidence: 81 clusters/13,301 enrolled, separate outcome denominators, SSI 16.1% versus18.9%, adjusted RR0.87, inseparable glove+instrument intervention, open abdominal population and 679 urology cases.
Qualified extrapolation of arthroplasty glove-change evidence to GU prostheses; no direct AUS/IPP/mesh infection-effect claim.
Made first-case latex-allergy scheduling conditional on powdered-latex exposure per ASCIA; retained latex-safe equipment and communication.

sources.access: Published PDF complete main text, tables, references, figure captions/text and funding/COI read. Figure graphics and supplement not independently viewed.

sources.notes: Twelve arthroplasty studies; none measured direct effect of glove-change policy on SSI/PJI. Contamination/perforation outcomes only.

Nine healthcare workers with accelerator allergy; supports formulation selection, not material-wide freedom from accelerators.
Latex allergy diagnosis and avoidance; updated operative environment anchored directly to ASCIA.
Two surgeons, repeated gloving, fluorescent contamination simulation; no SSI outcome.
Fluorescent contamination surrogate; no clinical zero-contamination or SSI guarantee.

unresolved: Full texts/supplements of Cochrane reviews and older material/donning/arthroplasty papers not accessed; conclusions limited to complete original abstracts and corroborating full consensus/guideline sections.
Enz and ChEETAh figure graphics/supplements not independently inspected; numerical results taken from main tables/text only.
No specific glove manufacturer IFU or institutional donning/implant-handling policy validated.
This automated scoped evidence review is not clinician approval or full verification of every possible clinical scenario.
